answer.location_description: The whole image: a periodic horizontal-stripe (line grating) pattern spanning every row and column. Rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, 12-13, 16-17 and 20-21 are bright; rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, 14-15, 18-19 and 22-23 are dark (period of 4 pixel rows).
answer.shortcut_type: Periodic horizontal stripe / scan-line artifact texture (period 4 rows) across the full image
answer.mechanism: Two families of first-layer units are matched horizontal gratings of opposite phase. Family A is units 8, 9, 10, 18, 20, 24, 27 and 29. They have large negative biases (-61 to -97) and weights that are positive on rows {0,1,4,5,...} and negative on rows {2,3,6,7,...}, so they fire only when that stripe phase is present. Family B is units 2, 3, 23 and 31. They have large positive biases (+65 to +99), the opposite phase, and are on by default; the stripe pattern switches them off. Family A feeds positively into layer-2 units u3, u4, u10, u12 and u13, whose output weights are +63, +77, +67, +42 and +71. Family A also feeds negatively into u1 and u7, whose output weights are -94 and -99. Family B does the reverse: it drives u1 and u7 and suppresses u3 and u13. The net effect is that the stripe pattern raises the malignant logit and its absence keeps the benign-leaning units u1 and u7 active.
answer.evidence: Unit 8: rows 0-1 are about +30, rows 2-3 about -30, rows 4-5 about +35, rows 6-7 about -40, and so on through row 21; the same alternation appears in units 9, 10, 18, 20, 24, 27 and 29. Units 2, 3, 23 and 31 show the inverted alternation: rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, 14-15, 18-19 and 22-23 are positive (40-88), the others negative. This alternation is uniform across all 24 columns, including the periphery far from the nodule. A pattern repeating exactly every 4 rows over the full field of view cannot be anatomy, because the images are rescaled per nodule so real structures have no fixed pixel period. Layer-2 weights from family A are strongly positive into u3, u4, u10, u12 and u13 (e.g. u13: 55, 99, 46, 31, 39, 63, 75; u4: 63, 63, 74, 83, 93) and strongly negative into u1 and u7 (e.g. u1: -73, -89, -66, -68). Output weights are positive for u3, u4, u10, u12 and u13 and -94 / -99 for u1 / u7. The remaining first-layer units (0, 4-7, 11-17, 19, 21, 22, 25, 26, 28, 30) look like unstructured noise.
answer.main_feature: Apart from the stripe detector, the grating units carry localized modulations near the nodule: a strong spot at rows 10-11, cols 16-19 and deviations around rows 12-15, cols 9-12. These suggest some sensitivity to nodule margin and density near the centre, but the genuine nodule signal is weak compared with the full-image stripe template.
